note: Monocrotaline rats predicted benefit for oral beraprost and ralinepag: beraprost's 12-week walk gain faded by 12 months, ralinepag later succeeded, and inhaled QCC374 stopped after eight patients.
label: PAH (IP receptor agonists)

engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the MCT rat readout is pulmonary artery pressure, whose human counterpart is right-heart-catheter haemodynamics.
engagement.note: Oral beraprost dose-dependently lowered pulmonary artery pressure in monocrotaline rats over three weeks.
engagement.short: Beraprost lowers Ppa in MCT rats
engagement.quote: We conclude that oral beraprost sodium suppresses pulmonary hypertension produced by monocrotaline in rat.

engagement.magnitude_basis: change in pulmonary haemodynamics at max tolerated beraprost dose vs ~15-17% Ppa fall in MCT rats
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); haemodynamics were a secondary endpoint. Uncontrolled Japanese series had reported acute haemodynamic falls.
engagement.judgement: Contra on beraprost's null haemodynamics in ALPHABET (secondary endpoint). Retrodiction rule (engagement and efficacy are target claims): epoprostenol, a PTGIR agonist, had already lowered pulmonary resistance and improved exercise in PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial (Rubin 1990, doi:10.7326/0003-4819-112-7-485), before this model was first public. It failed to reproduce the human result for beraprost, so contra with retrodiction true. Ralinepag's PVR fall is now its own track (appended entries).
engagement.note: At maximal tolerated doses for 12 weeks, beraprost did not significantly change pulmonary haemodynamics in 130 PAH patients. A retrodiction that failed to reproduce: prostacyclin had lowered pulmonary resistance in patients before the 1994 rat study.
engagement.quote: Cardiopulmonary hemodynamics and NYHA functional class had no statistically significant changes.
engagement.reason: Beraprost moved no haemodynamics in RCT

engagement.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;193:A2220), read in full; no full paper found.
engagement.note: Inhaled QCC374 reversed established vascular remodeling in MCT and Su5416/hypoxia rats.
engagement.quote: In vivo profiling of QCC374 via intratracheal administration in rats with established pulmonary vascular remodeling (following treatment with either monocrotaline (MCT) or Su5416 and held under chronic hypoxia (Hx/Su)) revealed potent anti-remodeling efficacy.

engagement.confidence_note: Registry results only (NCT02927366, posted 2019-08-07): Part I, 6 QCC374 vs 2 placebo, terminated for strategic reasons, descriptive analysis only.
engagement.judgement: Judgement call: untested (unsettled) rather than contra. PVR did not fall in the six treated patients, but n=6 vs 2 with descriptive analysis only cannot settle the comparison. Any comparison here would be a retrodiction: inhaled iloprost and treprostinil had already lowered PVR in PAH patients before 2016.
engagement.note: Week-16 PVR ratio to baseline was 1.07 on QCC374 (n=6) vs 1.05 on placebo (n=2); trial stopped after Part I.

engagement.model: Human platelet-rich plasma in vitro, ADP-induced aggregation (TRK-100/beraprost)
engagement.note: Beraprost (TRK-100) potently inhibited ADP-induced aggregation of human platelet-rich plasma in vitro.
engagement.short: Inhibits human platelet aggregation in vitro
engagement.quote: The drug was shown to be a potent inhibitor of platelet aggregation in vitro, induced by adenosine diphosphate (ADP), using platelet-rich plasma (PRP) from human and several animal species.

engagement.magnitude_basis: ex vivo ADP aggregation inhibition after 40-60 ug oral doses vs in vitro IC50 (no exposure-matched comparison)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Healthy volunteers; effect was brief (0.5-1 h) and poorly related to plasma APS-314d.
engagement.judgement: Paired by us: the in vitro human platelet readout (ADP aggregation) is the same readout measured ex vivo in dosed humans, so readout_tier direct. Retro, not same: prostacyclin (same target, same action) infused in volunteers induced ex vivo inhibition of platelet aggregation (PMID 6992228, 1980), so the 1985 in vitro model post-dates a known human result.
engagement.model: Human platelet-rich plasma in vitro, ADP-induced aggregation (TRK-100/beraprost)
engagement.note: Oral beraprost 40 and 60 ug inhibited ex vivo ADP-induced platelet aggregation in 12 healthy volunteers; 20 ug did not. Retrodiction: intravenous prostacyclin had already inhibited ex vivo platelet aggregation in volunteers (1980), before the 1985 in vitro model.
engagement.quote: BPS 40 and 60 micrograms decreased platelet aggregation 1 h after single doses, and 0.5 h and 1 h after repeated doses.
engagement.reason: Ex vivo platelet inhibition in volunteers

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC, PMID 28072531); readout of the rat model not given in the abstract.
engagement.judgement: Opener of the ralinepag track on the MCT rat, at the model's first use for this drug.
engagement.note: Ralinepag (APD811) showed oral efficacy in the monocrotaline rat model of PAH.
engagement.short: Ralinepag effective orally in MCT rats
engagement.quote: The design and synthesis of a new series of potent non-prostanoid IP receptor agonists that showed oral efficacy in the rat monocrotaline model of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) are described.

engagement.magnitude_basis: PVR -29.8% vs placebo at week 22 vs rat pulmonary pressure suppression
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC, PMID 31391223). Earliest public date: Arena topline press release, 10 Jul 2017 (reported by BioPharma Dive), before the ERJ paper (epub 2019-10-10) and registry results (2020-07-14).
engagement.judgement: Split from engagement 2 (ralinepag's patients differed in result from beraprost's). Retrodiction rule (engagement and efficacy are target claims): epoprostenol, a PTGIR agonist, had already lowered pulmonary resistance and improved exercise in PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial (Rubin 1990, doi:10.7326/0003-4819-112-7-485), before this model was first public. Year 2017 from the topline press release.
engagement.note: Phase 2: ralinepag lowered PVR 29.8% vs placebo in 61 PAH patients, as its MCT rat data implied; a retrodiction, since prostacyclin had lowered PVR in patients by 1990.
engagement.quote: Ralinepag significantly decreased PVR by 163.9 dyn·s·cm-5 compared to an increase of 0.7 dyn·s·cm-5 with placebo (p=0.02)
engagement.reason: Ralinepag lowered PVR, reproducing known result

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Ralinepag (Tran 2017) and beraprost doses in patients were set by titration to the maximal tolerated dose.
dose.judgement: All three members were titrated to individual tolerability in patients (beraprost median 80-120 ug QID; ralinepag up to 600 ug/day), so no model-stated target was tested.
dose.note: MCT rat studies gave oral mg/kg or drinking-water doses, no human exposure target or margin.
dose.quote: Rats were fed on distilled water (DW) or DW containing beraprost sodium (BPS).

dose.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;193:A2220), read in full; no full paper found.
dose.judgement: Judgement call: the hypotension-free window is scored in safety, not here, because no human exposure target was stated; Novartis's FIH (NCT02245828) basis is unpublished.
dose.note: Rat intratracheal doses defined a lung-to-systemic window but no human inhaled dose or exposure target was published.
dose.quote: Administration of increasing intratracheal doses of QCC374 to conscious, telemetered rats revealed no significant change in systemic blood pressure (sBP) at doses required to inhibit MCT or Hx/Suinduced pulmonary vascular remodeling.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Miyata 1996 (doi:10.1097/00005344-199601000-00004) reproduced it on RV hypertrophy.
efficacy.note: Beraprost suppressed monocrotaline pulmonary hypertension in rats, the proxy for benefit in PAH.
efficacy.quote: We conclude that oral beraprost sodium suppresses pulmonary hypertension produced by monocrotaline in rat.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 6MWD placebo-corrected +25.1 m vs rat Ppa suppression (different quantities)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Pre-registry trial; no NCT.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction rule (engagement and efficacy are target claims): epoprostenol, a PTGIR agonist, had already lowered pulmonary resistance and improved exercise in PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial (Rubin 1990, doi:10.7326/0003-4819-112-7-485), before this model was first public. The rat result reproduced ALPHABET's walk-distance benefit, so retro rather than same.
efficacy.note: ALPHABET met its primary endpoint: beraprost improved 6-minute walk by 25 m over placebo at 12 weeks. Retrodiction: prostacyclin had already improved PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial, before the 1994 rat study.
efficacy.quote: The difference between treatment groups in the mean change of 6-min walking distance at week 12 was 25.1 m (95% CI: 1.8 to 48.3, p = 0.036).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 12-month disease progression (primary) on beraprost vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Pre-registry trial; no NCT.
efficacy.judgement: Contra: the trial's primary endpoint at 12 months was not met. The 3-week MCT rat prevention designs could not speak to durability, but a benefit claim is scored on the trial's primary endpoint, so contra. Retrodiction rule (engagement and efficacy are target claims): epoprostenol, a PTGIR agonist, had already lowered pulmonary resistance and improved exercise in PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial (Rubin 1990, doi:10.7326/0003-4819-112-7-485), before this model was first public. Ralinepag's own MCT rat data (Tran 2017) and its patient results are now a separate track (appended entries).
efficacy.note: The US 12-month trial's primary endpoint (disease progression) failed: beraprost's benefit at 6 months faded by 9-12 months.
efficacy.quote: Patients treated with beraprost exhibited less evidence of disease progression at six months (p = 0.002), but this effect was not evident at either shorter or longer follow-up intervals.

efficacy.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;193:A2220), read in full; no full paper found.
efficacy.note: QCC374 anti-remodeling efficacy in MCT and Su5416/hypoxia rats was the benefit claim.
efficacy.quote: In vivo profiling of QCC374 via intratracheal administration in rats with established pulmonary vascular remodeling (following treatment with either monocrotaline (MCT) or Su5416 and held under chronic hypoxia (Hx/Su)) revealed potent anti-remodeling efficacy.

efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results only (NCT02927366, posted 2019-08-07): Part I, 6 QCC374 vs 2 placebo, terminated for strategic reasons, descriptive analysis only.
efficacy.judgement: PVR ratio 1.07 (QCC374) vs 1.05 (placebo) points against the rat prediction, but n=6 vs 2 without inference is not an admissible failure. Any comparison here would be a retrodiction: inhaled iloprost and treprostinil had already lowered PVR in PAH patients before 2016.
efficacy.note: Phase 2 primary (PVR at week 16) reported descriptively in 8 patients; program stopped for strategic reasons.

efficacy.population: WHO group 1 PAH on background inhaled treprostinil
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Co-authors include sponsor-side staff (von Kessler, Sista). Published May 2019, after BEAT primary completion (Feb 2019) but before results were posted (Feb 2020).
efficacy.judgement: Esuberaprost (BPS-314d) is the active stereoisomer within racemic beraprost, so it is treated as the member drug beraprost; a stricter reading of the member list would drop this track.
efficacy.model: PAH-patient PASMC proliferation and human distal pulmonary artery myography ex vivo (esuberaprost)
efficacy.note: Esuberaprost, beraprost's 314d isomer, inhibited proliferation of PAH-patient PASMCs (EC50 3 nM) and relaxed patient pulmonary arteries.
efficacy.quote: In human PASMCs, esuberaprost was 40-fold more potent than beraprost at inhibiting cell proliferation (EC50 3 nM versus 120 nM), contrasting the 5-fold potency difference for cAMP elevation.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: clinical worsening events, esuberaprost 49/136 vs placebo 51/135 (added to inhaled treprostinil)
efficacy.population: WHO group 1 PAH on background inhaled treprostinil
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry results (posted 2020-02-28) give event counts by component (8+23+7+6+5=49 vs 13+14+13+4+7=51) without inference; a 2026 Research Square preprint states 'There was no difference between treatment groups in time to clinical worsening (primary endpoint)'. No peer-reviewed paper found. Earliest public date: United Therapeutics press release 2019-04-08 (https://ir.unither.com/press-releases/2019/04-08-2019-145624946), 'BEAT Study of Esuberaprost Does Not Meet Primary Endpoint'.
efficacy.judgement: Combination trial scored on its primary endpoint, partner inhaled treprostinil in combination_with. The topline failure (press release 2019-04-08) predates Shen 2019 (epub 2019-05-31), so the ex vivo model is a retrodiction that did not reproduce it: contra, retrodiction true, year 2019 (checker adjudication).
efficacy.model: PAH-patient PASMC proliferation and human distal pulmonary artery myography ex vivo (esuberaprost)
efficacy.note: Combination design: esuberaprost added to inhaled treprostinil, scored on BEAT's primary (clinical worsening, 49 vs 51 patients of 271). Failure announced 8 Apr 2019, before the ex vivo paper: a failed retrodiction.
efficacy.short: BEAT: no effect on clinical worsening
efficacy.quote: The number of participants that experienced clinical worsening is presented; time to clinical worsening data was not measured.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC, PMID 28072531); readout of the rat model not given in the abstract.
efficacy.judgement: Opener of the ralinepag track on the MCT rat, at the model's first use for this drug.
efficacy.note: Ralinepag (APD811) showed oral efficacy in the monocrotaline rat model of PAH, the benefit claim for this drug.
efficacy.short: Ralinepag effective orally in MCT rats
efficacy.quote: The design and synthesis of a new series of potent non-prostanoid IP receptor agonists that showed oral efficacy in the rat monocrotaline model of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) are described.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: phase 2 primary PVR change vs rat MCT efficacy (different quantities)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC, PMID 31391223). Earliest public date: Arena topline press release, 10 Jul 2017 (reported by BioPharma Dive), before the ERJ paper (epub 2019-10-10) and registry results (2020-07-14).
efficacy.judgement: Split from efficacy 3 (ralinepag's patients differed in result from beraprost's). Retrodiction rule (engagement and efficacy are target claims): epoprostenol, a PTGIR agonist, had already lowered pulmonary resistance and improved exercise in PPH patients in a 1990 randomised trial (Rubin 1990, doi:10.7326/0003-4819-112-7-485), before this model was first public. PVR was the trial's primary; ADVANCE OUTCOMES (2026, positive) is the outcome trial and changes no status, so it sits in patient_trials.

patient_trials.quote: Overall, 64 (18%) of 350 patients in the ralinepag group and 121 (36%) of 337 patients in the placebo group had a first clinical worsening event (hazard ratio 0·45 [95% CI 0·33-0·62]; p<0·0001).

efficacy.reason: Ralinepag met primary, reproducing known result

safety.confidence_note: Conference abstract (Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2016;193:A2220), read in full; no full paper found.
safety.note: Telemetered rats showed no systemic blood-pressure fall at anti-remodeling inhaled doses: a predicted wide therapeutic window.
safety.short: No systemic BP fall in rats
safety.quote: Administration of increasing intratracheal doses of QCC374 to conscious, telemetered rats revealed no significant change in systemic blood pressure (sBP) at doses required to inhibit MCT or Hx/Suinduced pulmonary vascular remodeling.

safety.confidence_note: Registry results only (NCT02927366, posted 2019-08-07): Part I, 6 QCC374 vs 2 placebo, terminated for strategic reasons, descriptive analysis only. AE counts from the registry adverse-event table.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: untested. The rat prediction (no systemic BP fall) was not contradicted, yet flushing, headache, jaw pain and syncope are systemic prostanoid effects at odds with 'limited systemic vasodilation'; rats could not report headache or jaw pain, and n=6 settles neither way.
safety.note: No hypotension reported, but headache (5/6), flushing (3/6), jaw pain (2/6) and one syncope on QCC374 at 0.12 mg BID.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC, PMID 7825169). Galie 2002 and Barst 2003 abstracts report common drug-related prostacyclin adverse events but say nothing on systemic hypotension; full texts not reachable.
safety.judgement: Opener: the rat's unchanged systemic pressure at anti-PH doses is read as a no-systemic-hypotension prediction for beraprost.
safety.note: In MCT rats, oral beraprost suppressed pulmonary pressure without dose-dependently lowering systemic arterial pressure: a predicted pulmonary-selective window.
safety.short: No systemic pressure fall in rats
safety.quote: Psa was not lowered dose-dependently by BPS.

safety.magnitude_basis: systemic hypotension absent in patients at max tolerated doses vs no dose-dependent Psa fall in MCT rats
safety.confidence_note: Quote from Galie 2002 full text (Discussion), as verified by the checker; not re-read here. Prospective for the drug: no earlier beraprost patient hypotension result found.
safety.judgement: Pairing (comparison_stated false), checker adjudication: Yuki 1994 'Psa was not lowered' vs ALPHABET's absence of systemic hypotension. Headache, flushing and jaw pain are harms a rat cannot report, so its silence on them is not a miss.
safety.note: Paired: the rat's no-systemic-pressure-fall prediction held; at maximal tolerated doses ALPHABET saw no systemic hypotension in 130 PAH patients.
safety.quote: Despite the high doses of beraprost sodium used in this study, the safety profile of the drug was excellent with neither systemic hypotension nor hepatic, renal or hematologic side effects.
safety.reason: No hypotension in patients, as rats predicted
